subject: specify upper limit for a parameter

messages.author: 2b2a7dccb793ae6c
messages.subject: specify upper limit for a parameter
parts:
Dear Stan Users/Developers,
I have an array of parameter x[N], which follows truncated normal distribution. But the upper limit for each x is different, say the upper limits are U[N]. What is the script for declaring this parameter x? For now I tried two  ways, but neither of them works properly, see below. Thanks!

1. 
data{
    real U[N];
} 
parameters{
    real <lower=1> x[N];
}
model{
    for (i in 1:N)
        x[i] ~ normal(100,10) T[1, U[i]];
}

2. 
data{
    real U[N];
} 
parameters{
    real <lower=1, upper=U> x[N];
}
model{
    for (i in 1:N)
        x[i] ~ normal(100,10) T[1, U[i]];
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] specify upper limit for a parameter
parts:
You have to do the transform yourself and apply the Jacobian.

See section 20.4 of the manual. We hope to generalize the declarations
soon to allow this.

If you have a normal(100, 10), then you don't need the T[ , ]. Also,
if you do have explicit truncation with T[ , ], the bounds on the truncation
need to match those on the left-hand-side variable.

Scaling to unit scale usually works better computationally. Inits will be
at the mid-point of any hard range.

We generally recommend not imposing hard upper and lower bounds unless
dictated absolutely by the structure of the model (as in a parameter to
a binomial).

- Bob
